dispositions.disposition: Adopted. Freeze 002 freezes the launch and replaces stop rule 9. (a) Launch: every command runs as its shell member alone, read raw from the bound freeze with jq -r, with only its named placeholders replaced by their 64-hex values, in the shell tool's background mode with no tool timeout; one call per command, never retried. (b) The bound: in the same message the Director starts a frozen bound timer in the background, which exits at the first of the command's exit file existing or its outer_bound_s passing, prints which, starts only shell builtins, /bin/date and /bin/sleep, and writes nothing; its exact text is frozen, by digest if it is a file. (c) Stop rule 9 becomes FR-01's six steps: at the bound, record the overrun with its time, and the command's outcome is UNKNOWN; start one frozen capture_probe.py probe on every start pair the command has recorded so far (the runner's intent.json and started-<n>.json, the provider's preflight.json and started.json), the freeze listing every candidate pair and the rule that selects the recorded ones; run FC-P6's capture_probe.py stop only for a target in state 'present, identity established'; send nothing to the wrapper, the tool's task or its group (no kill, no task stop); wait for the wrapper to exit, then apply FAILURE-CAPTURE section 6, steps 5 to 7; if it never exits, the attempt stays UNKNOWN and the owner is told. (d) For C17, an FC-P6 stop of one case may be followed by the remaining CPU starts within C17 (FR-04). The review's further option, interrupting the overrunning tool itself, is not taken: it needs new procedure and tooling.
